papers.title_en: Training-Free Continual Learning for Multimodal Forecasting via Prompt Evolution
papers.authors: Laurent Mombaerts, Jonathan Taws, Jacopo Gargano, Dinesh Gaddam, Kevin George, Srijan Tiwari, Shreyas Rajesh
papers.evidence: 通过结果驱动反思进行提示词演化
papers.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于提示词演化的多模态时序预测免训练持续学习方法。通过结果驱动的反思机制动态演化文本指导块并输入冻结的大语言模型，在严格防范数据泄漏的基准测试中，该方法不仅超越了现有的时序基础模型，还将更新成本大幅降低。
papers.abstract_en: Adapting a forecasting system to a changing world classically means retraining. We ask whether the task of continually learning regimes for time series forecasting can be represented by a piece of text: a guidance block, evolved by outcome-driven reflection and used in a frozen LLM forecaster's prompt. On a refreshed multimodal benchmark (weekly search indices, daily currencies, daily commodities, each window paired with web-retrieved news), we run GEPA-style prompt evolution under strict contamination control to prevent the data leakage common in timeseries benchmarks: the forecaster's knowledge cutoff predates every evaluated window. A 900-word evolved guidance carried by Llama-3.3-70B beats TimeSeries Foundation Models (TSFMs) on held-out data (GM MASE 0.776 vs. 0.898 for TabPFN-TS-3), transfers to more recent models without measurable loss, and costs dollars rather than GPU-days to update. We characterize the loop: out-of-loop gains concentrate in the first reflection, in-loop improvements overstate out-of-loop gains 2-3x unless an untouched monitor arbitrates, and error-only objectives silently suppress the text modality. We provide two extensions. First, compiling the guidance into executable code with a TSFM as a callable tool recovers most of the gain deterministically. Second, ablations show the advantage widens at short horizons and that removing the news text does not hurt the guided forecaster, consistent with the text's value being distilled into policy during learning. We argue that continual prompt evolution is a practical, training-free alternative to retraining for multimodal forecasting.

papers.title_en: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Role-Enhanced Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Prompting
papers.authors: Ibrahim Khan, Thai Van Nguyen, Yi Xia, Pratch Suntichaikul, Mustafa Can Gursesli, Daniel Fernandez Galeote, Juho Hamari, Ruck Thawonmas
papers.evidence: 动态角色选择以实现自适应任务角色对齐
papers.tldr: 本文提出了角色增强的零样本思维链（RE-ZS-CoT）提示词框架，通过将领域特定的专家角色系统性地整合到大语言模型中，在无需特定任务示例的情况下显著提升了其推理能力。该方法在多个基准测试和模型上进行了广泛评估，展现出强大的性能提升与通用性。
papers.abstract_en: This paper proposes Role-Enhanced Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought (RE-ZS-CoT), a prompting framework that systematically integrates domain-specific expert roles to enhance reasoning in large language models (LLMs) without task-specific examples. We assess two versions of our approach. In the first version, static role selection, we evaluate eight predefined expert roles across arithmetic, commonsense, and reading comprehension benchmarks to determine their impact on reasoning performance. In the second version, dynamic role selection, each model autonomously selects the single most suitable role for each benchmark, enabling adaptive task-role alignment without manual specification. Across 20 LLMs and seven benchmarks, RE-ZS-CoT frequently surpasses zero-shot and zero-shot-CoT baselines, achieving performance improvements of up to 44 percentage points. The results reveal a strong correspondence between static and dynamic versions; the benchmarks where static roles yielded improvements were almost always those where dynamic roles also outperformed baselines, though static selection achieved peak performance. Ablation studies further show that unconventional roles degrade performance, underscoring the necessity of task-role alignment. The framework's scalability is validated across model sizes (2b-14b parameters), with smaller models like Granite3.3-8b achieving remarkable proficiency in arithmetic reasoning. RE-ZS-CoT advances zero-shot prompting by unifying role specialization with chain-of-thought reasoning, offering a practical, resource-efficient solution for improving LLM capabilities across diverse domains.

papers.authors: Karen Ji, Cameron Khanpour, Samuel Talkington, J. Kyle Skolfield, Daniel K. Molzahn
papers.evidence: 构建双层优化问题并使用梯度下降更新上层变量
papers.tldr: 极端天气下的电力系统规划需要明确输电线路故障的停电场景，但公开记录通常仅提供各县的停电客户数。为此，本文提出了一种新方法，利用区域减负荷数据恢复最吻合的故障输电线路集合。通过建立双层优化模型，将离散的线路状态松弛为概率并通过梯度下降法求解，再经随机舍入恢复整数性。实验表明，该方法能有效重建合理的输电网故障场景，为基于观测灾害的电力规划提供可靠数据。
papers.abstract_en: Expansion planning for extreme weather needs outage scenarios that specify which transmission branches fail. However, public outage records often only report customers without power by county, making it unclear how to exploit this information to create outage scenarios. We propose a method to recover sets of outaged branches that most closely match regional load shed data. This gives us sets of plausible outages for a given hazard event. We formulate a bilevel problem with a load shedding DC optimal power flow in the lower level. We relax the binary branch states to differentiate the lower level problem, replace it with its sensitivity matrix, and use gradient descent to update the upper level. We treat the relaxed branch states as probabilities and perform randomized rounding to restore integrality. On three test systems with synthetic outages, the recovered sets reduce the load shed error to $0.02-4.5\%$. On the California Test System with storm data from December 2025, the error falls to $23\%$. These scenarios give expansion planning a reliable source of outage data tied to observed hazards.

papers.title_en: Robust Soft Skill Adaptation via Behavioral Localization in Tool-Using Agents
papers.evidence: 通过行为定位监督短软提示
papers.tldr: 本文针对工具使用智能体中软提示词学习效率低与噪声干扰的问题，提出了行为定位（Behavioral Localization）方法。研究发现文本技能的作用高度集中于轨迹中的少数关键位置，通过对比冻结智能体在有无技能时的行为差异，精准识别并利用这些关键位置来监督简短的软提示词，从而在减少计算成本的同时显著提升了智能体性能。
papers.abstract_en: Text skills can extend the capabilities of tool-using agents, but long skill descriptions increase computational costs. Soft prompts provide a compact alternative, yet learning from entire successful trajectories may also introduce unnecessary behavioral changes. We find that the useful effect of a text skill is highly concentrated in a small subset of trajectory positions. Based on this observation, we propose Behavioral Localization, which compares the frozen agent with and without the text skill to identify positions where the skill both increases the likelihood of successful tokens and meaningfully changes the next token distribution. We use these localized positions to supervise a short soft prompt. Experiments on SpreadsheetBench with a frozen Qwen3.6-35B-A3B agent show that the top 10\% of trajectory positions capture 96.12\% of the total positive skill gain. In the shared prompt setting, selective supervision improves success from 30.36\% with full trajectory to 36.79\%. Under task-specific conditions, using the top 10\% localized positions achieves 57.38\%, outperforming both the full text skill and the on-policy OPCD baseline. These results show that a small set of behaviorally relevant trajectory positions can provide effective supervision of soft skills.

papers.title_en: Let Agents Design How They Search: Automatic Interface Optimization for Agentic Search
papers.authors: Sangjune An, Jaeyoon Jung, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek, Junmo Cho, Sung Ju Hwang, Hae Beom Lee
papers.evidence: 自动搜索界面优化，包括使用指令的优化
papers.tldr: 本文针对大模型智能体搜索中依赖固定、人工设计接口的局限，提出了SearchWeaver框架，通过下游搜索性能自动优化语料库工件、可执行工具和使用说明。实验表明，该方法显著提升了多个数据集上的搜索准确率和检索效果。
papers.abstract_en: Agentic search depends on the interface through which a language-model agent accesses and explores a corpus. Existing interface designs are fixed by hand and applied unchanged to every corpus, although effective designs may depend on the corpus. We introduce SearchWeaver, a framework for automatic search interface optimization guided by downstream search performance. A proposer uses execution trajectories and task rewards to jointly revise corpus artifacts, executable tools, and usage instructions. This pro cess optimizes what information is prepared in advance, which operations tools perform, and which decisions remain with the search agent. With GPT-5.4-nano, the optimized interfaces improve answer accuracy from 71.6% to 78.4% on BrowseComp-Plus and average nDCG@10 from 45.7 to 55.0 across four BRIGHT subsets over Direct Corpus Interaction. These findings highlight the value of jointly optimizing corpus artifacts, executable tools, and usage instructions to develop effective search interfaces.

papers.title_en: Mitigating Query Shortcuts in Chain-of-Thought with Context-Aware Decoding
papers.evidence: 思维链提示与推理优化
papers.tldr: 本研究针对大语言模型在思维链（CoT）推理中依赖查询捷径而非推理步骤的问题，提出了一种名为“推理对比解码”（RCD）的免训练方法。该方法利用上下文感知解码对比有无推理过程的输出分布，增强模型对推理内容的依赖，从而显著提升推理准确性。
papers.abstract_en: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), recent studies have shown that final answers do not always depend on the generated rationales. In particular, LLMs may rely on query-specific shortcuts rather than the information provided by their reasoning steps. In this paper, we investigate whether context-aware decoding (CAD), an existing contrastive decoding method, can mitigate such shortcut behavior when applied to CoT reasoning. We study this application as Rationale Contrastive Decoding (RCD), which contrasts the next-token distributions conditioned on the query with and without its rationale, amplifying tokens whose likelihood increases due to the rationale. We provide a theoretical interpretation of this decoding rule via a KL-regularized reward-maximization objective. Experiments across five reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that RCD improves answer accuracy over standard CoT. Furthermore, intervention analyses using ground-truth and random rationales reveal that RCD increases the behavioral dependence of final answers on the rationale content. Our findings suggest that contrastive decoding offers a simple, training-free approach to mitigating query shortcuts.

papers.title_en: S-EDL: Eliciting Self-Evidence from Sequence Likelihoods for Semantic Calibration of LLMs
papers.authors: Yawei Li, Jiazheng Li, David Rügamer, Bernd Bischl, Yulan He, Mina Rezaei
papers.evidence: 提示特定类别的可微狄利克雷先验
papers.tldr: 大语言模型在开放式生成中的语义校准面临挑战，因为同一语义可由多种不同词序列表达。为此，本文提出了S-EDL方法，通过从模型序列似然中提取证据，在可变语义类别上构建可微分的狄利克雷先验，实现对开放式生成的原生语义校准，在提升准确率的同时显著降低校准误差。
papers.abstract_en: Calibrating large language models (LLMs) in open-ended generation is uniquely challenging because many distinct token sequences can express the same underlying meaning. Prior calibration techniques target either fixed-set classification confidence or the binary correctness of individual strings, making them inherently ill-suited for the dynamic, multi-string nature of open-ended semantic outcomes. To bridge this gap, we introduce S-EDL, a novel evidential method that natively optimizes LLMs for semantic calibration. By eliciting evidence from the sequence likelihoods of the model itself, S-EDL constructs a differentiable Dirichlet prior over prompt-specific semantic classes. Optimizing the evidential loss under this prior yields a calibration-aware training signal over variable semantic classes, completely bypassing the need for fixed multiple-choice options. Evaluations across four open-ended benchmarks and three models demonstrate that S-EDL substantially reduces semantic calibration error while improving accuracy. By aligning generative likelihoods with semantic correctness, this work establishes a framework for deploying trustworthy LLMs in complex, open-ended applications. Code is available at: https://github.com/sandylaker/s-edl.

papers.title_en: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
papers.authors: Yunhao Luo, Wentao He, Yinpei Dai, Hyelin Nam, Hongze Fu, Joyce Chai, Nima Fazeli, Jeong Joon Park
papers.evidence: 通过上下文提示校准世界模型
papers.tldr: 现有的世界模型往往无法感知场景中决定过渡动力学的物理属性，导致预测产生严重漂移。为此，本文提出了PhysiCalWorld，通过上下文提示将动作条件世界模型校准到特定实例的动力学，无需微调或分析物理建模，显著提升了预测准确率和视觉规划成功率。
papers.abstract_en: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. Without calibrating these physics factors for world models, predictions tend to regress toward an empirical prior and induce severe drift in novel test scenes. To this end, we propose PhysiCalWorld, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling. Our method encodes an exploratory interaction clip collected within the test scene into a compact physics descriptor token, which grounds subsequent predictions in the scene's actual physical behavior. PhysiCalWorld is trained end-to-end with the latent prediction loss alone, without physics labels. At inference time, the descriptor token is extracted once and can be reused across rollouts with negligible compute overhead. We evaluate PhysiCalWorld across four environments covering diverse physics variations and show that it substantially improves rollout prediction accuracy and visual planning success rate. The learned descriptors also form a physically structured latent space and generalize beyond the physics ranges seen during training.

papers.title_en: Best of Both Worlds: Fine-Tuned Small Models Complement LLMs for Cost and Performance Benefits
papers.authors: Shivam Mathur, Sri Harish Popuri, Priya Krishnan Sundararajan, Kevin Horecka, Michael Mugo
papers.evidence: 探索 GPT-3.5 在文本分类中的最佳提示方法
papers.tldr: 本文探讨了微调小模型（如RoBERTa）与大语言模型（如GPT-3.5）在文本分类任务中的性能、成本和时间权衡。研究发现两者结合能实现优势互补，在大幅降低成本的同时提升分类准确率。
papers.abstract_en: BERT-based models require thousands of labeled samples to train. Larger models like GPT-X require only 1-5 examples per class. However, performance, cost and time tradeoffs of such models remain under-explored. In this work, we classify survey text data into 16 classes. We focus on experimental approaches and results on performance, cost, and time taken for this problem. We compare these parameters of a trained RoBERTa-based model, and an (off-the-shelf) GPT-3.5 model for text classification. Baseline experiments show that the time taken by GPT-3.5 for generating predictions on 10,000 records is 6 hours, whereas a RoBERTa-based model takes only 12 mins on a T4 GPU. To identify the best prompting approach for GPT-3.5, we explore batch prompting. We experiment with (1) batch-size, and (2) few-shot sampling. We find the best batch size is 20 with human few-shot curation. Experiments show the F1 score of a trained RoBERTa-based model (96%) is much higher than a GPT-3.5 model (83%). In case of GPT-3.5, batch prompting is beneficial in lowering inference costs by ~70%, without hindering task performance. We find the best approach is an ensemble of a RoBERTa-based and GPT-3.5 model (F1: 97.5%) incurring only 4.4% of inference cost compared to a standalone GPT-3.5.
